cases.reason: build a fixture project with each named location present and run the tool; each must be reported present, and none reported absent.
run the tool on a fixture with some named locations absent; any location listed as found that is not on disk fails it.
run the tool on a fixture with no AGENTS.md; the run must exit 1 and name AGENTS.md, not pass it.
run the tool with --project set to a git repo other than the current folder; the printed root must be that repo.
run the tool with --project set to a subfolder of a git repo; it must exit 2 as a usage error, not check the subfolder.
snapshot every file in a fixture, ignored ones included, before and after a run and diff them; only the report may differ.
run the tool on a fixture with known tool and git records and compare its checked list against the yaml; a decidable record missing from it fails.
run the tool on a fixture where a record's change is not visible to git or whose check is reviewer; it must give needs a reviewer, never pass or fail.
parse the report of a fixture run; every pass and fail line must carry a file and line or a command and its output.
parse the report of a fixture run; every result state must be one of the five.
run memory_index.py --check and the tool on a fixture whose index fails; the tool must not report a pass for that check.
only reading the tool's clause list against memory_index.py's checks can tell whether a clause is checked twice; a matching name is not enough.
run the tool on a fixture with no project-memory/ folder; every requirement must be not applicable with the absent location named, and none may fail.
run the tool on a staged fixture and on a history range; the report's first line must name the snapshot and the range.
run the tool on a fixture with a cache folder; B2.2 and Rd1 must each show pass or fail, not be absent from the report.
run the tool on a fixture with a cache folder; the other CACHES requirements must show needs a reviewer, not pass or fail.
run the tool and compare the requirement ids in the report against the C1 records; any missing id fails it.
run the tool's checks output and the report on the same fixture; the results must match item for item.
run --warn on a fixture with a failing MUST; that MUST's id must appear in the warning.
run --warn on a fixture with failing MUSTs and a missing AGENTS.md; any line beyond those, or any entry text, fails it.
run the hook's command on a fixture with a cache file present under a file-open trace; any open of a cache file fails it.
run the tool on a fixture with a failing MUST; the exit code must be 1, not 0.

whether the expected bytes were written by hand or by an engine that did not write the check is not visible in the files, so only the author or EJ can confirm it; the code-reading part alone would be judged.
run the tool on a fixture and diff the whole memory tree and cache before and after; any change other than the report fails it.
run the tool on a fixture and check that each pass line carries its evidence; a pass without evidence fails it.
run the tool under a file-open trace with decoy transcript and credential files present; any open of them fails it, and the whole-tree part is not covered by this trace.
only reading whether the tool's index check calls memory_index.py or rebuilds its checks can tell whether it replaces that tool.
